question: Which native change and identity contracts should providers reuse for local, remote and reconnect behavior?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles hard-cut comparison; bounded synchronization, provider, presence and Plate consumer review
trigger: User requested the next Best API Review ledger item. Selected order 10, collaboration. Review and local evidence recording only; independent Plate feature reviews remain separate.
requirements: Accepted canonical changes remain the document truth; discarded transaction specs and aborted editor updates must not publish requested external effects.
Preserve CRDT convergence, schema admission, named roots, mapped selections, history policy and shared authored effects across local, remote and reconnect paths.
Do not overwrite an unsynchronized provider room with placeholder editor content; establish coherent document identity, readiness and seeding authority.
Transport can outlive a mounted editor; awareness is transient, and cursor mapping and geometry respect the mounted view.
Keep product presentation and room/auth policy in the app or copied UI; retain inferred cursor-data contracts and one native configuration owner.
Assess collaboration's 12 mapped census groups without absorbing independent feature reviews or implementing the recommended target.
evidenceReuse: Initial collaboration record. Rechecked current raw binding, provider and awareness adapters, Plate authoring/decoration, local peer and Hocuspocus examples, copied UI, and native detached-transaction contracts. Earlier entrypoint and cursor-presentation plans provide context only; no historical proof or adjacent authored/core verdict is inherited. Replayed 77 existing tests plus two diagnostic cases. Sequential review; no independent worker claim.
summary: Pursue cutting the editor transport-command facade and Plate's duplicate Yjs configuration store while retaining one native document binding. A current-source probe confirms cursor publication, pause and disconnect from both discarded transaction specs and aborted updates despite zero commits and unchanged text. Transport/presence and document acceptance need explicit lifetime ownership, coherent readiness/seed identity and error handling. Preserve canonical Yjs imports, shared effects and exact-view cursor presentation. Task design plan owns the coupled contract, adoption and proof decisions; this review does not settle a final API.
alternatives: Keep/configure: existing options do not prevent immediate transport and presence effects during discarded or aborted transaction work; insufficient.
Stage existing tx.yjs calls after acceptance: viable correctness repair and required comparison baseline, but retains transport/admin/profile operations inside document transactions.
Change existing contracts: pursue one configuration owner plus explicit readiness and presence lifetimes; reuse existing commit/lifecycle mechanisms before adding machinery.
Add generic collaboration/session service: reject without an independent user job; a minimal supplied readiness adapter may be justified by actual providers.
Delete/merge Plate's configuration store: pursue removing the nullable duplicate Yjs option representation while preserving Plate authoring, cursor-data inference and selection decoration.

Delete editor transport facade: strongest candidate; provider/app owns connection, failures and teardown, while native binding observes the capabilities required for safe synchronization. Do not shift sync-gating boilerplate into every app.
Delete awareness or store it in document content: reject because transient selection/profile state has independent expiry, view lifetime and undo semantics.
Move all collaboration into Plate: reject; raw Plite consumers need neutral synchronization and cursor reads, while product appearance remains with copied UI.
Replace Yjs with generic local-change or snapshot broadcast: reject as the default target; local path changes alone do not provide offline/concurrent convergence or relative identity.
Replace event bridge/shared-effect log/cursor cache: no demonstrated wholesale rewrite case. Any changed runtime machinery requires a named deficiency and matched executable scale comparison.
proofLimits: 69 existing Plite provider/awareness/schema/multi-root tests pass in four files; eight Plate adapter tests pass in one file. Two source-backed diagnostic cases reproduce external effects from discarded specs and aborted updates. Probe setup errors were corrected and documented. No real network/server, browser/native device, performance comparison, full CRDT/history soak or proposed implementation was executed. Census review is bounded API/architecture coverage, not exhaustive behavioral coverage. Inventory refresh updates observations only and does not refresh older reviews. Detailed readiness, async lifetime, seeding, inference and adoption proof remains open.
